heading.en: Steel or rubber: which is more elastic?
heading.kn: ಉಕ್ಕು ಅಥವಾ ರಬ್ಬರ್: ಯಾವುದು ಹೆಚ್ಚು ಸ್ಥಿತಿಸ್ಥಾಪಕ?

hook.en: Most people say rubber. A physicist says steel, because it needs a far bigger stress to produce the same strain.
hook.kn: ಹೆಚ್ಚಿನವರು ರಬ್ಬರ್ ಎನ್ನುತ್ತಾರೆ. ಭೌತವಿಜ್ಞಾನಿ ಉಕ್ಕು ಎನ್ನುತ್ತಾನೆ, ಏಕೆಂದರೆ ಅದೇ ವಿಕೃತಿಗೆ ಉಕ್ಕಿಗೆ ಬಹಳ ಹೆಚ್ಚು ಪ್ರತಿಬಲ ಬೇಕು.

title.en: Define Young's modulus and use Y = FL/(AΔL)
Describe Searle's method of finding Y

say.en: Most people say rubber. A physicist says steel, because it needs a far bigger stress to produce the same strain. In this lesson: Define Young's modulus and use Y equals FL over Adelta L.
Describe Searle's method of finding Y.

body.en: *Young's modulus* is the ratio of longitudinal (tensile or compressive) stress to longitudinal strain: Y = (F/A)/(ΔL/L) = FL/(AΔL). Its unit is the pascal. Metals have large values: steel about 2 × 10¹¹ Pa, copper about 1.2 × 10¹¹ Pa, aluminium about 7 × 10¹⁰ Pa. A larger Y means the material is harder to stretch.
body.kn: ಯಂಗ್‌ನ ಗುಣಾಂಕ = ನೀಳ ಪ್ರತಿಬಲ ÷ ನೀಳ ವಿಕೃತಿ = FL/(AΔL). ಏಕಮಾನ ಪ್ಯಾಸ್ಕಲ್. ಉಕ್ಕಿಗೆ ಸುಮಾರು 2 × 10¹¹ Pa. Y ದೊಡ್ಡದಾದಷ್ಟು ವಸ್ತುವನ್ನು ಹಿಗ್ಗಿಸುವುದು ಕಷ್ಟ.

say.en: Young's modulus is the ratio of longitudinal tensile or compressive stress to longitudinal strain: Y equals (F over A)/(delta L over L) equals FL over Adelta L. Its unit is the pascal. Metals have large values: steel about 2 times 10 to the power 11 pascals, copper about 1.2 times 10 to the power 11 pascals, aluminium about 7 times 10 to the power 10 pascals. A larger Y means the material is harder to stretch. Y depends only on the material and temperature.

say.en: Extension delta L equals FL over AY.
Searle's apparatus: two identical wires hang from one support. The reference wire keeps the scale steady; the experimental wire carries the load.
Young's modulus is longitudinal stress divided by longitudinal strain.
With load Mg on a wire of radius r, the area is pi r squared.
Steel wire, 2 metre long, radius half a millimetre, load 10 kilogram. The extension is only about 1.25 millimetre: that is why we need a micrometer.
Plot load against extension. It is a straight line; its slope gives Y. A steeper line means a stiffer wire.

narration.en: Add masses one at a time and watch the extension. The points fall on a straight line (Hooke's law), and stress ÷ strain is the same at every load: that constant is Young's modulus Y = FL/(AΔL). A thicker or shorter wire stretches less, but Y belongs to the material.

say.en: Let us solve this together. A steel wire 2 metres long and of radius 1 millimetre carries a load of 100 kilograms. Find its extension. (Y equals 2 times 10 to the power 11 pascals, g equals 9.8 metres s to the power minus 2).
F equals 100 times 9.8 equals 980 newtons; A equals pi (1 times 10 to the power minus 3) squared equals 3.14 times 10 to the power minus 6 square metres.
delta L equals FL over AY equals 980 times 2 / (3.14 times 10 to the power minus 6 times 2 times 10 to the power 11).
delta L equals 1960 / (6.28 times 10 to the power 5) is approximately 3.1 times 10 to the power minus 3 metres.
So the answer is About 3.1 millimetres.

body.en: For the same material and load, ΔL ∝ L/A ∝ L/r². If a wire is stretched by drawing it (volume fixed), A ∝ 1/L, so ΔL ∝ L².

homework.en: A copper wire 3 m long, area 2 mm², stretches 1.2 mm under 96 N. Find Y for copper.

narration.en: Recap. Y = stress/strain = FL/(AΔL), in pascal. Y is a property of the material, not of the wire size. Searle's method uses a reference wire and a spirit level.
narration.kn: ಪುನರಾವರ್ತನೆ. Y = ಪ್ರತಿಬಲ/ವಿಕೃತಿ = FL/(AΔL). Y ವಸ್ತುವಿನ ಗುಣ; ತಂತಿಯ ಗಾತ್ರವನ್ನು ಅವಲಂಬಿಸುವುದಿಲ್ಲ. ಸರ್ಲ್‌ನ ವಿಧಾನದಲ್ಲಿ ಆಧಾರ ತಂತಿ ಮತ್ತು ಸ್ಪಿರಿಟ್ ಲೆವೆಲ್ ಬಳಸುತ್ತೇವೆ.

say.en: Let us recall the key ideas. Y equals stress/strain equals FL over Adelta L, in pascal.
say.kn: ಮುಖ್ಯ ಅಂಶಗಳನ್ನು ನೆನಪಿಸಿಕೊಳ್ಳೋಣ. Y equals ಪ್ರತಿಬಲ/ವಿಕೃತಿ = FL over Adelta L.

say.en: Y is a property of the material, not of the wire size.
say.kn: Y ವಸ್ತುವಿನ ಗುಣ; ತಂತಿಯ ಗಾತ್ರವನ್ನು ಅವಲಂಬಿಸುವುದಿಲ್ಲ.
